prompt: Draw the chessboard position of the Italian Game after 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4, as a single self-contained SVG diagram. A square 8x8 board seen from White's side: a1 dark and bottom-left, rank 8 at the top, file letters a-h along the bottom edge and rank digits 1-8 along the side edge, a border frame around the whole board. All 32 starting men are still on the board, each one drawn as real vector geometry in the classic Staunton silhouette (pawn, rook, knight, bishop, queen, king each unmistakably its own shape), never as a letter or a glyph. White's e-pawn stands on e4, knight on f3 and bishop on c4; Black's e-pawn stands on e5 and knight on c6. Beside the board, a panel gives the move list 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4, names the opening as the Italian Game, and says that it is Black to move.
definition_of_done: final_output_file: chess-opening.svg, a single self-contained SVG. All 14 cases in test_acceptance.py pass via `python -I -m unittest discover -s . -v` with exit code 0. (1) The file parses as XML, the root is <svg>, and its viewBox holds 4 numbers with width and height of at least 100. (2) Elements carry exactly these ids: board, frame, squares, files, ranks, pieces, panel, caption, moves, tomove. (3) The document contains no <script>, no <image> and no <foreignObject>. (4) It makes zero external requests: no http(s) or protocol-relative href/src, no @import, no url(//...). (5) The 64 squares are <rect id="sq-XY"> with numeric x/y/width/height forming an exact 8x8 grid: every square the same size within 1%, square within 1%, each on its file column and rank row within 2% of the side, rank 8 at the top, and the board's overall width equal to its height within 1%. (6) Every square carries a literal #rrggbb fill, all 32 squares of a1's colour share one value, all 32 of the other colour share one other value, and a1's is the darker of the two by relative luminance. (7) Eight <text id="file-a"> ... <text id="file-h"> read exactly their own letter and sit horizontally within their own column, and eight <text id="rank-1"> ... <text id="rank-8"> read exactly their own digit and sit vertically within their own row. (8) Inside id=pieces there is one element id="piece-<square>" for each of the 32 occupied squares of the position after 3.Bc4 and no others, each carrying data-piece set to its two-letter code (wP, wN, wB, wR, wQ, wK, bP, bN, bB, bR, bQ, bK). (9) Every piece group carries transform="translate(cx,cy)" landing on the centre of its own square within 5% of the square's side. (10) No <text>, <tspan> or <use> appears inside id=pieces, and every piece is drawn with at least 2 shape elements, at least one of which is a <path>. (11) All six piece types appear, and no two types share the same geometry signature, so a knight is not a rook with another fill. (12) Every piece group carries a hex fill, and the darkest white piece is lighter than the lightest black piece by more than 0.2 of relative luminance. (13) id=moves exists and holds id=move-1 containing e4 and e5, id=move-2 containing Nf3 and Nc6, id=move-3 containing Bc4; id=caption names the Italian; id=tomove says Black. (14) <rect id="panel"> has numeric x/y/width/height, lies entirely outside the board's column span, and sits wholly inside the viewBox.
contract: Produce ONE SVG document in the `code` field, starting with <svg and ending with </svg>. The root <svg> needs xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" and a viewBox of 4 numbers. Tag the semantic parts with these exact ids: board (the whole board group), frame (the border drawn around the board), squares (the group holding the 64 cells), files (the group of file letters), ranks (the group of rank digits), pieces (the group holding the men), panel (a <rect> for the side panel), caption (the text naming the opening), moves (the group holding the move list), tomove (the text saying whose move it is). Each cell is <rect id="sq-<file><rank>"> for all 64 of a1..h8, with numeric x, y, width, height and a literal #rrggbb fill; a1 is the dark colour and sits bottom-left, rank 8 at the top. Labels are <text id="file-a">a</text> through file-h and <text id="rank-1">1</text> through rank-8, each with a numeric x (files) or y (ranks). Each man is <g id="piece-<square>" data-piece="wP" fill="#rrggbb" transform="translate(cx,cy)"> whose children draw the piece around the local origin (0,0); the two-letter data-piece code is w or b followed by P N B R Q K. Piece geometry is real vector outline: at least two shapes per piece, at least one <path>, and no <text>, <tspan> or <use> anywhere under id=pieces, so every piece carries its own geometry. The move list holds <g id="moves"> with <text id="move-1">, <text id="move-2">, <text id="move-3">. The panel rect must not overlap the board's column span and must stay inside the viewBox. Forbidden: <script>, <image>, <foreignObject>, any external reference (http(s) or protocol-relative href/src, @import, url(//...)), any CSS or font or library loaded from outside the file, and any animation. Self-contained, static, vector only.

import re
import unittest
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
from pathlib import Path

TARGET = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "chess-opening.svg"

FILES = "abcdefgh"
RANKS = "12345678"

# The Italian Game after 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4: square -> colour+type code.
POSITION = {
    "a1": "wR", "b1": "wN", "c1": "wB", "d1": "wQ", "e1": "wK", "h1": "wR",
    "a2": "wP", "b2": "wP", "c2": "wP", "d2": "wP", "f2": "wP", "g2": "wP",
    "h2": "wP", "e4": "wP", "f3": "wN", "c4": "wB",
    "a8": "bR", "c8": "bB", "d8": "bQ", "e8": "bK", "f8": "bB", "g8": "bN",
    "h8": "bR", "a7": "bP", "b7": "bP", "c7": "bP", "d7": "bP", "f7": "bP",
    "g7": "bP", "h7": "bP", "e5": "bP", "c6": "bN",
}
REQUIRED_IDS = {"board", "frame", "squares", "files", "ranks", "pieces",
                "panel", "caption", "moves", "tomove"}
SHAPES = {"path", "circle", "ellipse", "rect", "polygon", "polyline", "line"}
TRANSLATE = re.compile(r"translate\(\s*(-?[\d.]+)[\s,]+(-?[\d.]+)\s*\)")
GEOM_ATTRS = ("d", "points", "cx", "cy", "r", "rx", "ry", "x", "y",
              "width", "height", "x1", "y1", "x2", "y2")


def tag(el):
    return el.tag.split("}")[-1]


def num(value, default=None):
    try:
        return float(str(value).strip())
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return default


def lum(color):
    """Relative luminance of a #rrggbb colour, or None if it is not one."""
    m = re.match(r"^#([0-9a-fA-F]{6})$", (color or "").strip())
    if not m:
        return None
    h = m.group(1)
    r, g, b = (int(h[i:i + 2], 16) / 255.0 for i in (0, 2, 4))
    return 0.2126 * r + 0.7152 * g + 0.0722 * b


def text_of(el):
    return "".join(el.itertext()).strip()


class Acceptance(unittest.TestCase):
    @classmethod
    def setUpClass(cls):
        cls.raw = TARGET.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        cls.root = ET.fromstring(cls.raw)
        cls.byid = {}
        for el in cls.root.iter():
            ident = el.get("id")
            if ident:
                cls.byid.setdefault(ident, el)

    # --- helpers --------------------------------------------------------
    def el(self, ident):
        node = self.byid.get(ident)
        self.assertIsNotNone(node, "missing id=%s" % ident)
        return node

    def square(self, name):
        """(x, y, width, height) of the <rect id="sq-XY"> for one square."""
        node = self.el("sq-" + name)
        vals = [num(node.get(k)) for k in ("x", "y", "width", "height")]
        for value, key in zip(vals, ("x", "y", "width", "height")):
            self.assertIsNotNone(value, "sq-%s needs a numeric %s" % (name, key))
        return vals

    def grid(self):
        return {f + r: self.square(f + r) for f in FILES for r in RANKS}

    def pieces(self):
        holder = self.el("pieces")
        found = {}
        for node in holder.iter():
            ident = node.get("id") or ""
            if ident.startswith("piece-"):
                found.setdefault(ident[len("piece-"):], node)
        self.assertTrue(found, "no piece-<square> elements inside id=pieces")
        return found

    def signature(self, node):
        """Geometry only: what the piece is drawn as, ignoring its colours."""
        parts = []
        for child in node.iter():
            if tag(child) not in SHAPES:
                continue
            bits = [tag(child)]
            for key in GEOM_ATTRS:
                bits.append(re.sub(r"\s+", " ", (child.get(key) or "").strip()))
            parts.append("|".join(bits))
        return "\n".join(parts)

    # --- 1-4: the document ---------------------------------------------
    def test_root_is_svg_with_viewbox(self):
        self.assertEqual(tag(self.root), "svg")
        box = (self.root.get("viewBox") or "").replace(",", " ").split()
        self.assertEqual(len(box), 4, "viewBox must have 4 numbers, got %r" % box)
        w, h = num(box[2]), num(box[3])
        self.assertTrue(w and w >= 100, "viewBox width too small: %r" % w)
        self.assertTrue(h and h >= 100, "viewBox height too small: %r" % h)

    def test_required_ids_present(self):
        missing = sorted(REQUIRED_IDS - set(self.byid))
        self.assertEqual(missing, [], "missing required ids: %s" % missing)

    def test_no_script_or_raster(self):
        kinds = {tag(el) for el in self.root.iter()}
        self.assertNotIn("script", kinds, "SVG must not contain <script>")
        self.assertNotIn("image", kinds, "SVG must be vector only, no <image>")
        self.assertNotIn("foreignObject", kinds)

    def test_no_external_references(self):
        for el in self.root.iter():
            for key, value in el.attrib.items():
                if key.split("}")[-1] in ("href", "src") and re.match(r"\s*(https?:)?//", value or ""):
                    self.fail("external reference in %s: %s" % (tag(el), value))
        self.assertNotIn("@import", self.raw)
        self.assertFalse(re.search(r"url\(\s*['\"]?(https?:)?//", self.raw),
                         "external url() reference")

    # --- 5-7: the board -------------------------------------------------
    def test_board_is_an_exact_eight_by_eight_grid(self):
        geom = self.grid()
        widths = [g[2] for g in geom.values()]
        heights = [g[3] for g in geom.values()]
        side = widths[0]
        self.assertGreater(side, 0, "squares have no size")
        self.assertLessEqual(max(widths) - min(widths), 0.01 * side,
                             "squares are not all the same width")
        self.assertLessEqual(max(heights) - min(heights), 0.01 * side,
                             "squares are not all the same height")
        self.assertLessEqual(abs(max(heights) - side), 0.01 * side,
                             "squares are not square: %s wide, %s tall" % (side, max(heights)))
        x0 = min(g[0] for g in geom.values())
        y0 = min(g[1] for g in geom.values())
        for name, (x, y, _, _) in geom.items():
            fi, ri = FILES.index(name[0]), RANKS.index(name[1])
            self.assertLessEqual(abs(x - (x0 + fi * side)), 0.02 * side,
                                 "sq-%s is not in file column %s" % (name, name[0]))
            self.assertLessEqual(abs(y - (y0 + (7 - ri) * side)), 0.02 * side,
                                 "sq-%s is not in rank row %s (rank 8 must be at the top)"
                                 % (name, name[1]))
        width = max(g[0] for g in geom.values()) + side - x0
        height = max(g[1] for g in geom.values()) + side - y0
        self.assertLessEqual(abs(width - height), 0.01 * max(width, height),
                             "board is not square: %s x %s" % (width, height))

    def test_squares_alternate_and_a1_is_dark(self):
        dark, light = set(), set()
        for f in FILES:
            for r in RANKS:
                fill = (self.el("sq-" + f + r).get("fill") or "").strip().lower()
                self.assertRegex(fill, r"^#[0-9a-f]{6}$",
                                 "sq-%s%s needs a literal hex fill, got %r" % (f, r, fill))
                same_as_a1 = (FILES.index(f) + RANKS.index(r)) % 2 == 0
                (dark if same_as_a1 else light).add(fill)
        self.assertEqual(len(dark), 1, "dark squares must share one colour: %s" % sorted(dark))
        self.assertEqual(len(light), 1, "light squares must share one colour: %s" % sorted(light))
        d, l = lum(dark.pop()), lum(light.pop())
        self.assertLess(d, l,
                        "a1 must be the dark colour: a1 luminance %.3f vs h1 %.3f" % (d, l))

    def test_file_and_rank_labels_match_the_grid(self):
        for f in FILES:
            node = self.el("file-" + f)
            self.assertEqual(text_of(node), f, "file-%s must read %r" % (f, f))
            x, _, side, _ = self.square(f + "1")
            lx = num(node.get("x"))
            self.assertIsNotNone(lx, "file-%s needs a numeric x" % f)
            self.assertTrue(x <= lx <= x + side,
                            "file label %s at x=%s is not over column %s-%s" % (f, lx, x, x + side))
        for r in RANKS:
            node = self.el("rank-" + r)
            self.assertEqual(text_of(node), r, "rank-%s must read %r" % (r, r))
            _, y, _, high = self.square("a" + r)
            ly = num(node.get("y"))
            self.assertIsNotNone(ly, "rank-%s needs a numeric y" % r)
            self.assertTrue(y <= ly <= y + high,
                            "rank label %s at y=%s is not beside row %s-%s" % (r, ly, y, y + high))

    # --- 8-12: the pieces ----------------------------------------------
    def test_position_is_the_italian_game_after_three_bc4(self):
        found = self.pieces()
        self.assertEqual(sorted(found), sorted(POSITION),
                         "occupied squares do not match the position after 3.Bc4")
        for name, code in sorted(POSITION.items()):
            self.assertEqual((found[name].get("data-piece") or "").strip(), code,
                             "piece-%s should be %s" % (name, code))

    def test_every_piece_is_centred_on_its_square(self):
        for name, node in sorted(self.pieces().items()):
            m = TRANSLATE.search(node.get("transform") or "")
            self.assertIsNotNone(m, "piece-%s needs transform=\"translate(cx,cy)\"" % name)
            px, py = float(m.group(1)), float(m.group(2))
            x, y, w, h = self.square(name)
            self.assertLessEqual(abs(px - (x + w / 2.0)), 0.05 * w,
                                 "piece-%s off centre in x: %s vs %s" % (name, px, x + w / 2.0))
            self.assertLessEqual(abs(py - (y + h / 2.0)), 0.05 * h,
                                 "piece-%s off centre in y: %s vs %s" % (name, py, y + h / 2.0))

    def test_pieces_are_drawn_shapes_not_letters(self):
        holder = self.el("pieces")
        written = [tag(el) for el in holder.iter() if tag(el) in ("text", "tspan")]
        self.assertEqual(written, [], "pieces must be drawn, not written as letters")
        borrowed = [el for el in holder.iter() if tag(el) == "use"]
        self.assertEqual(borrowed, [], "each piece must carry its own geometry, no <use>")
        for name, node in sorted(self.pieces().items()):
            drawn = [c for c in node.iter() if c is not node and tag(c) in SHAPES]
            self.assertGreaterEqual(len(drawn), 2,
                                    "piece-%s is drawn with only %d shape(s)" % (name, len(drawn)))
            self.assertTrue(any(tag(c) == "path" for c in drawn),
                            "piece-%s has no <path>: a real piece outline is expected" % name)

    def test_the_six_piece_types_have_distinct_shapes(self):
        rep = {}
        for name, node in sorted(self.pieces().items()):
            code = (node.get("data-piece") or "")[1:2].upper()
            rep.setdefault(code, (name, self.signature(node)))
        self.assertEqual(sorted(rep), list("BKNPQR"),
                         "expected all six piece types, got %s" % sorted(rep))
        items = sorted(rep.items())
        for i in range(len(items)):
            for j in range(i + 1, len(items)):
                self.assertNotEqual(items[i][1][1], items[j][1][1],
                                    "%s and %s are drawn with the same shape"
                                    % (items[i][0], items[j][0]))

    def test_white_and_black_pieces_are_distinguishable(self):
        sides = {"w": [], "b": []}
        for name, node in sorted(self.pieces().items()):
            code = (node.get("data-piece") or "")[:1]
            self.assertIn(code, sides, "piece-%s has no w/b colour code" % name)
            value = lum(node.get("fill"))
            self.assertIsNotNone(value, "piece-%s needs a hex fill on its group" % name)
            sides[code].append(value)
        self.assertTrue(sides["w"] and sides["b"], "both sides must be on the board")
        self.assertGreater(min(sides["w"]), max(sides["b"]) + 0.2,
                           "white pieces (%.3f) and black pieces (%.3f) are too close in tone"
                           % (min(sides["w"]), max(sides["b"])))

    # --- 13-14: the side panel ------------------------------------------
    def test_panel_lists_the_moves_and_names_the_opening(self):
        self.el("moves")
        for ident, tokens in (("move-1", ("e4", "e5")),
                              ("move-2", ("Nf3", "Nc6")),
                              ("move-3", ("Bc4",))):
            txt = text_of(self.el(ident))
            for token in tokens:
                self.assertIn(token, txt, "%s should contain %r, got %r" % (ident, token, txt))
        self.assertIn("italian", text_of(self.el("caption")).lower(),
                      "the caption must name the opening")
        self.assertRegex(text_of(self.el("tomove")).lower(), r"black",
                         "after 3.Bc4 it is Black to move")

    def test_panel_sits_beside_the_board(self):
        panel = self.el("panel")
        px, py, pw, ph = [num(panel.get(k)) for k in ("x", "y", "width", "height")]
        for value, key in zip((px, py, pw, ph), ("x", "y", "width", "height")):
            self.assertIsNotNone(value, "panel needs a numeric %s" % key)
        geom = self.grid()
        side = geom["a1"][2]
        x0 = min(g[0] for g in geom.values())
        x1 = max(g[0] for g in geom.values()) + side
        self.assertTrue(px >= x1 or px + pw <= x0,
                        "panel (%s-%s) overlaps the board (%s-%s)" % (px, px + pw, x0, x1))
        box = (self.root.get("viewBox") or "").replace(",", " ").split()
        vw, vh = num(box[2]), num(box[3])
        self.assertTrue(0 <= px and px + pw <= vw, "panel is outside the viewBox")
        self.assertTrue(0 <= py and py + ph <= vh, "panel is outside the viewBox")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()
